findings.summary: Prior final-review major (rf-f639e6ef: directory-entry sync obligation lost after Journal reconstruction) is addressed. load() no longer treats a readable journal file as durability-proof; it calls _recover_sync_duty(path), which keeps the file out of _files_synced and repopulates _created_dirs with the ancestor chain, so the next _persist_append re-syncs the file's own parent entry plus every created ancestor's parent entry before acking. Two offline tests pin the reconstruction window (test_reconstruction_re_syncs_the_directory_chain, test_reconstruction_recovers_a_crashed_repair_rename).

Mechanical identity read-only check: the supplied input_commit, subject_commit and implementation_subject_commit are the same full SHA (4371704e...); implement handoff records work_head_commit 9e1c3e... with compileall exit 0 and focused pytest 110 passed (recorded, not independently re-run). Live Runtime/ReAct binding, reply delivery, process stop/resume, full Session query, integration/deploy and joint E2E remain deferred under development-stage constraints and are not grounds for this verdict.

Cosmetic: the _files_synced docstring still claims a file enters after 'load observes a file that already survived to disk'; load now deliberately keeps reconstructed files out of _files_synced. Correctness-neutral documentation drift only.
